docs.title: How to read this document
docs.text:
• All wins are in credits. The bet is 10 credits.
  • "x bet" means a multiple of the bet.
  • A symbol name in capital letters (for example KEY) is a technical name. The glossary gives the definitions.
  • KEY is the technical name of the collect symbol. The playable game shows this symbol as a fishing hook and uses the name HOOK.
  • The tables come from the configuration file. A script writes them. Thus the numbers agree with the game.

docs.title: Writing standard
docs.text: This document uses the writing rules of ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English) for most of the text. The sentences are short. The verbs are in the active voice and in simple tenses. One word has one meaning. Full compliance is not a goal of this issue. The tables, the formulas and the game names are outside the standard.

docs.title: How to change the configuration
docs.text:
There are two procedures.

Procedure A: change the JSON file.

  1. Change the values in config/game_config.json.
  2. If you changed the reel recipe, run python3 gamemath/gen_reels.py.
  3. Run python3 gamemath/exact_calc.py --json build/theo.json.
  4. Run .venv/bin/python tools/build_excel.py.
  5. Run .venv/bin/python tools/gen_docs.py.

Procedure B: change the Excel workbook.

  1. Change the yellow cells in the workbook. The workbook shows the new RTP immediately.
  2. Save the workbook.
  3. Run .venv/bin/python tools/excel_to_config.py.
  4. Do steps 3 and 5 of procedure A.

Procedure C: try a change in the game.

The demo suite of the playable game has the tool "Math configuration". It shows the configuration as JSON. You can change values there and apply them in the game. This change is for a test only. It stays in the browser and does not change the file.

docs.title: Excel Calculation in Detail
docs.text:
This page explains each sheet, each block and each formula of the workbook excel/TacklinTheKraken_TheoCalc.xlsx. The page Excel workbook gives the short instructions. This page gives the full calculation.

The cell addresses and the formula texts on this page come from the workbook file. The numbers are the results for math version 2.7.0.

docs.title: 1. Structure of the calculation
docs.text:
The workbook has 12 sheets. The data moves in one direction, from the inputs to the sheet Summary:

   Config    Reels_Base    Reels_Bonus     inputs (yellow cells)
                    |
                    v
          Win_Base    Win_Bonus            symbol counts for each stop
                    |
                    v
         Ways    Fish    Trigger           expected values, probabilities
                    |
                    v
                  Bonus                    free spins
                    |
                    v
                 Summary                   RTP, key figures, checks

              Distribution                 simulation values (separate)

The diagram shows the sequence of the calculation. The table gives the exact sources of each sheet.

Sheet Reads from Gives Config no other sheet All number inputs Reels_Base, Reels_Bonus no other sheet for the strips. The check cells read the symbol list and the placement rules of Config, and the FS column of the Win sheet. The reel strips and the reel strip checks Win_Base Reels_Base The number of each symbol in the window, for each stop of each base reel Win_Bonus Reels_Bonus The same for the bonus reels Ways Win_Base, Win_Bonus, Config (paytable, bet) Expected ways pays for the base reels and for the bonus reels Fish Win_Base, Win_Bonus, Config (fish values, weights, bet) Expected collect for the base game and for each level Trigger Win_Base, Config (initial free spins) Probability of 3, 4 and 5 FS symbols Bonus Win_Bonus, Ways, Fish, Trigger, Config (levels, multipliers, multiplier rule, bet) Level probabilities and the expected value of the free spins Summary Ways, Fish, Trigger, Bonus, Reels_Base, Reels_Bonus, Config (bet) RTP, key figures and checks Distribution no other sheet Win distribution tables from the simulation ReadMe no other sheet Short instructions

The calculation has these steps:

Step Sheet Function 1 Config, Reels_Base, Reels_Bonus Inputs. You change the yellow cells. 2 Win_Base, Win_Bonus Count each symbol in the window, for each stop of each reel. 3 Ways Expected ways pays for each pay symbol. 4 Fish Expected KEY and FISH collect for the base game and for each level. 5 Trigger Probability of 3, 4 and 5 FS symbols. 6 Bonus Probability of each level and expected value of the free spins. 7 Summary RTP, key figures and checks.

All results are formulas. The workbook has no macros and no values that a person must copy.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Colours. Yellow cells are inputs. Grey cells are fixed by the layout. Green cells are results or checks. Orange cells are fixed values from an external calculation (the script gamemath/exact_calc.py or the simulation). They are not formulas.
  • Units. All values are credits. The RTP is the expected win divided by the bet.
  • Stops. Stop s shows strip positions s, s+1, s+2 and s+3. Each stop has the probability 1/100.
  • Division by 100. A formula that divides by Config!$B$6 calculates a mean or a probability for the 100 stops of one reel.
  • Fixed layout. The workbook is made for 5 reels, 4 rows and 100 symbols for each reel.

This sheet holds all number inputs.

An empty cell means "no value". Input Fish value weights C33:F52 One row for each mode and FISH symbol. Weight n belongs to value n. Rows are in groups of 4: base, level 1, level 2, level 3, level 4. Level 1 has the text "initial" for its spins. Input Multiplier rule B68 all: the multiplier applies to ways pays and collect. fish: collect only. Input (list) Placement rules, base reels B73:F79 One row for each special symbol, one column for each reel. 1 = permitted, 0 = not permitted. The reel sheet checks are made for these values. Fixed

The placement rules do not change the RTP. They only control the checks on the reel sheets.

docs.title: 3. Sheets Reels_Base and Reels_Bonus
docs.text: The two sheets have the same layout. Reels_Base holds the base reel strips. Reels_Bonus holds the bonus reel strips.

docs.title: Reel strips
docs.text:
• Cells B4:F103 hold the 100 symbols of reels 1 to 5. Row 4 is stop 0. Row 103 is stop 99. Column A shows the stop number.
  • Each cell has a list of the permitted symbol names. A special symbol has a blue background.
  • Rows 104 to 106 are the wrap rows. They repeat the first 3 symbols of the strip, so that a window at the end of the strip can read its symbols in one range:
Reels_Base!B104:  =B4
Reels_Base!B105:  =B5
Reels_Base!B106:  =B6

docs.title: Check columns
docs.text:
Columns Rows Contents Formula (reel 1, first row) H:L 4 to 106 1 if the symbol is a special symbol =IF(COUNTIF(Config!$H$21:$H$27,B4)>0,1,0) N:R 4 to 103 1 if the gap rule is broken: the symbol is special and one of the next 3 symbols is special =IF(AND(H4=1,(H5+H6+H7)>0),1,0) T:X 4 to 103 1 if the symbol name is not in the symbol list =IF(COUNTIF(Config!$H$11:$H$27,B4)=0,1,0) AM:AQ 4 to 106 1 if the symbol is an AUS symbol =IF(COUNTIF(Config!$H$16:$H$20,B4)>0,1,0) AS:AW 4 to 103 1 if this position starts more than 3 AUS symbols in sequence =IF(SUM(AM4:AM7)=4,1,0)

The gap check and the AUS check read the wrap rows. Thus they are also correct at the end of the strip.

docs.title: Symbol counts and checks
docs.text:
Cells Contents Formula (first cell) Z4:Z20 The 17 symbol names text AA4:AE20 Number of each symbol on each reel strip =COUNTIF(B$4:B$103,$Z4) AA21:AE21 Number of symbols on the strip =SUM(AA4:AA20) AG4:AK20 1 if a special symbol is on a reel where the placement rules do not permit it =IF(AND(AA14>0,Config!$B$73=0),1,0) (row 14, FISH1) AA24:AE24 Check: the strip does not have 100 symbols =IF(AA21=Config!$B$6,0,1) AA25:AE25 Check: number of stops that break the gap rule =SUM(N4:N103) AA26:AE26 Check: number of unknown symbols =SUM(T4:T103) AA27:AE27 Check: number of placement rule violations =SUM(AG4:AG20) AA28:AE28 Check: number of stops that show two FS symbols =COUNTIF(Win_Base!$R$4:$R$103,">1") AA29:AE29 Check: number of positions that start too many AUS symbols in sequence =SUM(AS4:AS103) AA30 Result of all checks: OK or CHECK =IF(SUM(AA24:AE29)=0,"OK","CHECK")

A check value of 0 means "no violation". The checks do not stop the calculation. The RTP formulas use the strips as they are.

docs.title: 4. Sheets Win_Base and Win_Bonus
docs.text:
These helper sheets are the base of all subsequent formulas. One row is one stop. One column is one symbol on one reel. The cell gives the number of that symbol in the 4-row window at that stop.

  • Row 3 holds the symbol names. Rows 4 to 103 are stops 0 to 99.
  • Each reel has a block of 17 columns. The sequence of the symbols in a block is: PIC1, PIC2, PIC3, PIC4, PIC5, AUS1, AUS2, AUS3, AUS4, AUS5, FISH1, FISH2, FISH3, FISH4, KEY, WILD, FS.
Reel Columns First column (PIC1) KEY column WILD column FS column 1 B to R B P Q R 2 S to AI S AG AH AI 3 AJ to AZ AJ AX AY AZ 4 BA to BQ BA BO BP BQ 5 BR to CH BR CF CG CH

Each cell counts one symbol in a range of 4 cells on the reel sheet:

Win_Base!B4:  =COUNTIF(Reels_Base!$B4:$B7,B$3)
Win_Base!AX4:  =COUNTIF(Reels_Base!$D4:$D7,AX$3)
Win_Base!CE103:  =COUNTIF(Reels_Base!$F103:$F106,CE$3)

The last example is the last stop of reel 5. Its range goes into the wrap rows.

From these counts, the other sheets get three types of results with three formula patterns:

Result Formula pattern Mean number of a symbol in the window SUM(column) / 100 Probability of exactly k symbols in the window COUNTIF(column, k) / 100 Mean of the product of two counts on the same reel SUMPRODUCT(column 1, column 2) / 100

docs.title: 5. Sheet Ways
docs.text:
The sheet has two blocks with the same layout. Rows 5 to 14 are the base reel strips. Rows 20 to 29 are the bonus reel strips. One row is one pay symbol.

Columns Contents Formula in row 5 (PIC1, base reels) B:F M(r): mean number of the symbol or WILD in the window of reel r =(SUM(Win_Base!$B$4:$B$103)+SUM(Win_Base!$Q$4:$Q$103))/Config!$B$6 G:K Z(r): probability that the window of reel r shows no such symbol and no WILD =SUMPRODUCT(--((Win_Base!$B$4:$B$103+Win_Base!$Q$4:$Q$103)=0))/Config!$B$6 L:P Expected number of ways for exactly 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 of a kind =B5*C5*D5*J5 (column N, 3 of a kind) Q:U Paytable values from the sheet Config =Config!$D$11 (column S, 3 of a kind) V:Z Expected value for each of a kind number = expected ways x pay =N5*S5 (column X, 3 of a kind) AA Expected value of the symbol =SUM(V5:Z5) AB RTP of the symbol =AA5/Config!$B$3 AC:AG Probability of exactly 1 to 5 of a kind (for information) =(1-G5)*(1-H5)*(1-I5)*J5 (column AE, 3 of a kind)

The expected ways for 1 to 5 of a kind in row 5 are:

Ways!L5:  =B5*H5
Ways!M5:  =B5*C5*I5
Ways!N5:  =B5*C5*D5*J5
Ways!O5:  =B5*C5*D5*E5*K5
Ways!P5:  =B5*C5*D5*E5*F5

The product of the mean counts is correct because the reels are independent. The factor Z of the subsequent reel makes sure that the combination ends there. Column P has no factor Z, because a combination cannot continue after reel 5.

The totals are in AA15 and AB15 (base reels) and in AA30 and AB30 (bonus reels):

Ways!AA15:  =SUM(AA5:AA14)
Ways!AB15:  =AA15/Config!$B$3
Ways!AA30:  =SUM(AA20:AA29)

docs.title: Mean fish values, cells B5:E9
docs.text:
One row is one mode (base, level 1 to level 4). One column is one FISH symbol. The mean value is the sum of value x weight, divided by the sum of the weights:

Fish!B5:  =SUMPRODUCT(Config!$B$25:$E$25,Config!$C$33:$F$33)/SUM(Config!$C$33:$F$33)
Fish!E9:  =SUMPRODUCT(Config!$B$28:$E$28,Config!$C$52:$F$52)/SUM(Config!$C$52:$F$52)

docs.title: KEY and FISH counts, rows 14 to 20 (base reels) and 25 to 31 (bonus reels)
docs.text:
Columns Contents Formula in row 14 (reel 1, base reels) B E[k(r)]: mean number of KEY symbols in the window of the reel =SUM(Win_Base!$P$4:$P$103)/Config!$B$6 C:F E[n(r, f)]: mean number of FISH1 to FISH4 in the window of the reel =SUM(Win_Base!$L$4:$L$103)/Config!$B$6 G:J E[k(r) x n(r, f)]: mean of the product for the same reel =SUMPRODUCT(Win_Base!$P$4:$P$103,Win_Base!$L$4:$L$103)/Config!$B$6

Row 19 (row 30 for the bonus reels) is the sum of the 5 reels. Row 20 (row 31) is the expected number of KEY and FISH pairs in the full window, E[K x N(f)]:

Fish!C20:  =$B$19*C19-SUMPRODUCT($B$14:$B$18,C14:C18)+G19
Fish!F31:  =$B$30*F30-SUMPRODUCT($B$25:$B$29,F25:F29)+J30

The formula has three parts:

  1. $B$19*C19 is (sum of the KEY means) x (sum of the FISH means). This is correct for a KEY and a FISH on different reels. It is not correct for the same reel.
  2. -SUMPRODUCT($B$14:$B$18,C14:C18) removes the part for the same reel.
  3. +G19 adds the correct value for the same reel, from the product of the counts at each stop.

docs.title: Collect EV, rows 36 to 40
docs.text:
One row is one mode. Row 36 is the base game and uses row 20. Rows 37 to 40 are levels 1 to 4 and use row 31.

Fish!C36:  =B5*C20
Fish!G36:  =SUM(C36:F36)
Fish!H36:  =G36/Config!$B$3
Fish!C37:  =B6*C31
Fish!G40:  =SUM(C40:F40)

Each cell in C:F is (mean value of the FISH symbol in the mode) x (expected number of pairs). Column G is the collect EV of one spin, before the level multiplier.

Cell FISH symbol Mean value E[K x N(f)] EV (credits) C36 FISH1 1.9995 0.064000 0.127968 D36 FISH2 13.4500 0.019200 0.258240 E36 FISH3 60.5000 0.004800 0.290400 F36 FISH4 548.3871 0.004800 2.632258

G36 = 3.308866 credits. This is the collect EV of the base game.

docs.title: FS symbols for each reel, rows 5 to 9
docs.text:
Columns B, C and D give the probability of 0, 1 and 2 FS symbols in the window of the reel. Column E is the sum. The sum must be 1.

Trigger!B5:  =COUNTIF(Win_Base!$R$4:$R$103,0)/Config!$B$6
Trigger!C5:  =COUNTIF(Win_Base!$R$4:$R$103,1)/Config!$B$6
Trigger!D5:  =COUNTIF(Win_Base!$R$4:$R$103,2)/Config!$B$6
Trigger!E5:  =SUM(B5:D5)

docs.title: Number of FS symbols in the full window, rows 14 to 18
docs.text:
Row 14 is the distribution after reel 1. Each subsequent row adds one reel. Columns D to N are the totals 0 to 10. Columns B and C are zero "pad" columns for the formulas at the left edge.

Trigger!D14:  =B5
Trigger!G15:  =G14*$B$6+F14*$C$6+E14*$D$6
Trigger!G18:  =G17*$B$9+F17*$C$9+E17*$D$9

The formula in row 15 reads: the probability of a total of k after reel 2 = (total k after reel 1) x P(0 on reel 2) + (total k-1) x P(1 on reel 2) + (total k-2) x P(2 on reel 2). Row 18 is the distribution for all 5 reels.

docs.title: Trigger probabilities, rows 23 to 26
docs.text:
Trigger!B23:  =G18
Trigger!B24:  =H18
Trigger!B25:  =SUM(I18:N18)
Trigger!B26:  =SUM(B23:B25)
Trigger!C26:  =IF(B26>0,1/B26,"")
Trigger!D23:  =Config!$B$57
Cell Meaning Value B23 P(3 FS symbols) 0.00555827 B24 P(4 FS symbols) 0.00026214 B25 P(5 or more FS symbols) 0.00000492 B26 Trigger probability 0.00582533 C26 Trigger frequency 1 in 171.66

docs.title: KEY symbols in one free spin, rows 5 to 22
docs.text:
Rows 5 to 9 and rows 14 to 18 use the method of the sheet Trigger, with the KEY columns of Win_Bonus. Row 18 is the distribution of the number of KEY symbols in one free spin (columns D to N = 0 to 10).

Bonus!B5:  =COUNTIF(Win_Bonus!$P$4:$P$103,0)/Config!$B$6
Bonus!D18:  =D17*$B$9+C17*$C$9+B17*$D$9
Bonus!D20:  =N18
Bonus!N20:  =D18
Bonus!B22:  =SUMPRODUCT(D13:N13,D18:N18)

Row 20 holds the same distribution in the opposite direction (10 to 0). The state tables use this row. B22 is the mean number of KEY symbols for each free spin (0.2000).

docs.title: State tables, from row 47
docs.text:
The state tables calculate the probability to play each level. The state is the total number of KEY symbols in the free spins.

  • Row 47 is the header. Columns M to AL are the states 0 to 25. The last column means "25 or more". Columns C to L are empty pad columns.
  • A block has one title row and 41 spin rows (spin 0 to spin 40). Column B shows the spin number.
  • A cell gives the probability that the free spins are in this level, after this number of spins of the level, with this total number of KEY symbols.
Block Title row Spin rows (spin 0 to spin 40) Level 1 (all triggers) 48 49 to 89 Level 2 after a 3 FS trigger 91 92 to 132 Level 3 after a 3 FS trigger 134 135 to 175 Level 4 after a 3 FS trigger 177 178 to 218 Level 2 after a 4 FS trigger 220 221 to 261 Level 3 after a 4 FS trigger 263 264 to 304 Level 4 after a 4 FS trigger 306 307 to 347 Level 2 after a 5 FS trigger 349 350 to 390 Level 3 after a 5 FS trigger 392 393 to 433 Level 4 after a 5 FS trigger 435 436 to 476

Level 1, spin 0. The free spins start with 0 KEY symbols. Cell M49 is 1. The other cells of the row are 0.

One spin. Each spin row comes from the row above it:

Bonus!M50:  =SUMPRODUCT(C49:M49,$D$20:$N$20)
Bonus!P50:  =SUMPRODUCT(F49:P49,$D$20:$N$20)
Bonus!AL50:  =SUM($M49:$AL49)-SUM($M50:$AK50)
  • The SUMPRODUCT multiplies 11 cells of the row above (states k-10 to k) with the reversed KEY distribution in row 20. The result is the sum of P(state k-j) x P(j KEY symbols in one spin) for j = 0 to 10.
  • For the first states, the range starts in the empty pad columns. An empty cell counts as 0.
  • The last column takes the remaining probability: the total of the row above minus the other cells of the row. Thus the total of a row stays the same during a level.

Start of the subsequent level. The spin 0 row of a level 2, 3 or 4 block takes the row at the end of the level before it. It keeps only the states at or above the threshold:

Bonus!M92:  =IF(M$47>=Config!$B$64,INDEX(M$49:M$89,Config!$B$57+1),0)
Bonus!P92:  =IF(P$47>=Config!$B$64,INDEX(P$49:P$89,Config!$B$57+1),0)
Bonus!P135:  =IF(P$47>=Config!$B$65,INDEX(P$92:P$132,Config!$C$64+1),0)
  • INDEX(range, n + 1) reads the row after n spins. For level 2, n is the number of initial free spins (Config!$B$57 for a 3 FS trigger) and the range is the level 1 block. For level 3, n is the number of spins of level 2 and the range is the level 2 block of the same trigger.
  • The IF sets a state below the threshold to 0. These states are the free spins that end.
  • The sum of the spin 0 row is the probability to play the level.

The level 1 block is the same for all triggers. The triggers use different rows of it (after 10, 15 or 20 spins).

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
• Each reel stops at one of 100 stop positions. Each stop position has the same probability.
  • The reels are independent.
  • The window of a reel at stop s is the strip positions s to s+3.

For each reel r and each symbol X, the calculation uses the count c(r, X). This is the number of symbols X in the window. The calculation finds c(r, X) for each of the 100 stops.

docs.title: Ways pays
docs.text:
For a pay symbol S, let n(r) be the number of S symbols plus the number of WILD symbols in the window of reel r.

The symbol S gives exactly k of a kind when n(1) to n(k) are more than zero and n(k+1) is zero. The number of ways is then n(1) x n(2) x ... x n(k).

The reels are independent. Thus the expected number of ways is a product:

E[ways for exactly k OAK] = M(1) x M(2) x ... x M(k) x Z(k+1)      for k = 1 to 4
E[ways for exactly 5 OAK] = M(1) x M(2) x M(3) x M(4) x M(5)

M(r) = mean of n(r) for the 100 stops of reel r
Z(r) = fraction of the 100 stops of reel r where n(r) = 0

EV(S)   = sum for k = 1 to 5 of  pay(S, k) x E[ways for exactly k OAK]
EV ways = sum of EV(S) for all pay symbols

The product is correct because the term n(1) x ... x n(k) is zero when one of the counts is zero.

Condition

The formula is correct only if reel 1 has no WILD symbol. With a WILD symbol on reel 1, one way can pay for more than one symbol. The engine and the workbook reject such a strip.

docs.title: Example: PIC1 on the base reel strips
KEY and FISH collect
docs.text:
Let K be the number of KEY symbols in the window. Let N(f) be the number of FISH symbols of type f in the window. Let V(f) be the mean value of FISH type f in the current mode.

The value of each FISH symbol is independent of the stop positions. Thus:

EV collect = sum for all FISH types f of  V(f) x E[K x N(f)]

K and N(f) are sums of the reel counts. Counts on different reels are independent. Counts on the same reel are not independent.

E[K x N(f)] = (sum of E[k(r)]) x (sum of E[n(r, f)])
              - sum for each reel r of E[k(r)] x E[n(r, f)]
              + sum for each reel r of E[k(r) x n(r, f)]

k(r)    = number of KEY symbols in the window of reel r
n(r, f) = number of FISH type f symbols in the window of reel r

The last term uses the 100 windows of the reel directly. This formula is correct for KEY symbols on all reels.

docs.title: Level probabilities
docs.text:
The state of the free spins is the total number of KEY symbols, k. The calculation holds the probability of each state. The top state is "9 or more".

  1. Level 1 starts with probability 1 in state k = 0.
  2. For each spin, the calculation moves the probability from state k to state k + j. The factor is the probability of j KEY symbols in one spin.
  3. At the end of a level, the states below the threshold of the next level stop. Their probability leaves the calculation.
  4. The sum of the probabilities that stay is the probability to play the next level.
  5. The calculation does steps 2 to 4 again for each level.
P(play level 1) = 1
P(play level L) = sum of the state probabilities with k >= threshold(L), at the end of level L-1

The win of a spin in level L is independent of the event "the player gets to level L". That event depends only on the spins before level L. Thus the expected values multiply:

EV(bonus | trigger t) = sum for all levels L of  P(play level L | t) x spins(L, t) x spin EV(L)
EV(bonus per base spin) = sum for all triggers t of  P(t) x EV(bonus | t)

docs.title: Reel strip generator
docs.text:
The script gamemath/gen_reels.py makes the reel strips from a recipe. The recipe gives the number of each symbol on each reel. The generator uses a fixed seed for the base reel strips (803) and a fixed seed for the bonus reel strips (374). Thus the result is repeatable. A different seed gives a different arrangement of the same symbols. The arrangement changes the RTP of the ways pays a little, and it changes the number of spins with a win. See Tuning history.

The generator does these steps for each reel:

  1. It puts the special symbols in a random sequence. The spaces between them are the spans.
  2. It makes stacks of PIC symbols and puts them into the spans. A stack has 3 symbols or less.
  3. It makes groups of 1 to 3 AUS symbols. It puts one group at most into each position between two PIC stacks or adjacent to a special symbol. Thus two AUS groups never touch.
  4. It gives AUS groups first to the spans that have fewer than 3 pay symbols.
  5. It makes sure that the strip obeys all requirements. If not, it starts again.

docs.title: Symbol weighting on each reel
docs.text:
Each PIC symbol and each AUS symbol has its own pattern. It has more symbols on some reels and fewer symbols on other reels. Thus the reels are different from each other.

Symbol Pattern Base reel strips: symbols on reels 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 Bonus reel strips: symbols on reels 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 PIC1 Few symbols on reel 2 (base reel strips) and on reel 3 (bonus reel strips) 7 / 2 / 4 / 6 / 5 12 / 7 / 3 / 10 / 9 PIC2 Most symbols on the last reels 5 / 6 / 6 / 9 / 11 5 / 8 / 9 / 11 / 12 PIC3 Most symbols on the middle reels 6 / 10 / 11 / 10 / 6 7 / 11 / 14 / 11 / 7 PIC4 Most symbols on the outer reels 11 / 9 / 5 / 7 / 12 14 / 10 / 6 / 10 / 14 PIC5 Most symbols on reels 1 and 3 13 / 6 / 12 / 6 / 9 17 / 8 / 16 / 7 / 12 AUS1 Most symbols on the last reels 6 / 10 / 10 / 12 / 14 6 / 10 / 14 / 15 / 15 AUS2 Most symbols on the first reels 14 / 12 / 10 / 9 / 6 14 / 14 / 13 / 9 / 6 AUS3 Most symbols on reels 2 and 4 7 / 15 / 6 / 13 / 9 5 / 12 / 7 / 9 / 7 AUS4 Most symbols on reels 1 and 3 15 / 7 / 13 / 7 / 10 2 / 2 / 3 / 2 / 2 (no pattern) AUS5 Most symbols on the middle reels 7 / 12 / 13 / 11 / 8 1 / 1 / 3 / 1 / 2 (no pattern)

The bold numbers are the reels that the pattern favours.

  • When a symbol has most of its symbols on the first reels, a win of this symbol starts frequently. Few of these wins continue to reel 5.
  • When a symbol has most of its symbols on the last reels, a win of this symbol starts less frequently. More of these wins continue to reel 5.
  • Base reel 2 has 2 PIC1 symbols and 3 WILD symbols. Thus a PIC1 win starts rarely. Of the stops of base reel 2 that continue a PIC1 way, 71% show a WILD symbol. PIC1 has the largest pays.
  • On the bonus reel strips, AUS4 and AUS5 have 3 symbols or fewer on each reel. They have no pattern there.
  • The special symbols have no pattern. The requirements and the math model give their numbers.

The patterns came with version 2.1.0. Before that version, each PIC symbol had the same number of symbols on each reel of a reel set. The pattern of PIC1 changed with versions 2.3.0, 2.4.0 and 2.5.0. See Tuning history.

docs.title: Fast simulator
docs.text:
The program sim_cpp/krakensim is a C++ simulator for very large runs. It reads the same configuration file and plays the same game.

  • It plays approximately 90 million rounds for each second on one processor core. On 18 cores, it plays approximately 1.1 billion rounds for each second.
  • The JavaScript simulator plays approximately 5 million rounds for each second on 18 cores.
  • One reel stop is one 32-byte record. A spin reads five records. The program examines only the pay symbols that can make a paying combination.
  • The program selects FISH values only when a KEY symbol is in the window, and only for the FISH symbols in the window. The values are independent of the stop positions. Thus the win distribution is the same as in the game engine.
  • The script sim_cpp/crosscheck.py gives the same reel stops to the C++ program and to the JavaScript engine. All results of 100,000 spins were equal.
  • The run for this document played 1,000,000,000,000 rounds in 965 seconds (16.1 minutes) on 18 threads. It gave an RTP of 96.2010% with a standard error of 0.0009%. The exact RTP is 96.2000%.
  • Each thread starts on a different seed. Thread 0 uses the seed of the --seed option. Each subsequent thread uses the next number. The program prints the seeds and writes them to the result file.
  • The program writes the same result file as the JavaScript simulator. Thus --json build/sim.json puts its results into this document and into the workbook.

  • The last column is 1 divided by the cumulative probability: one free spins feature in this number has such a win.

docs.title: Game Rules
docs.text: This page gives all rules of the game. A person who reads this page can calculate the result of each spin. The examples use real stop positions of the reel strips. A script calculates each example.

docs.title: 1. The game in brief
docs.text:
• The game has 5 reels and 4 rows. It pays for 1024 ways.
  • One base spin costs the bet of 10 credits.
  • Pay symbols pay for ways from reel 1 to the right. WILD helps to make ways.
  • FISH symbols show credit values. A KEY symbol collects the values of all FISH symbols in the window. The game shows the KEY symbol as a fishing hook and calls it HOOK.
  • 3, 4 or 5 FS symbols start the free spins. The free spins have 4 levels. Each level has a multiplier. KEY symbols open the subsequent level.
  • All wins are in credits.

docs.title: 2. Bet and game round
docs.text:
1. The bet is 10 credits for each base spin. The player cannot change the number of ways.
  2. A game round starts when the player starts a base spin. The game subtracts the bet from the balance.
  3. A game round has one base spin. If the base spin starts the free spins, the game round also has all free spins.
  4. Free spins do not cost a bet.
  5. The win of a game round is the sum of the win of the base spin and the wins of all free spins.
  6. The game adds the win to the balance. The game has no win limit.

docs.title: 3. Reels and window
docs.text:
1. Each reel has a reel strip of 100 symbols. The reel strip is a loop: position 0 follows position 99.
  2. A spin selects one stop position for each reel. Each of the 100 stop positions has the same probability. The reels are independent.
  3. The stop position is the strip position of row 1 (the top row). Rows 2, 3 and 4 show the subsequent strip positions.
  4. The window is the 20 symbols that the player sees: 4 symbols on each of the 5 reels.
  5. The game has two sets of reel strips. The base game uses the base reel strips. The free spins use the bonus reel strips. The page Reel strips shows all strips.
  6. On each reel strip there are 3 or more pay symbols between two special symbols. Thus the window of one reel shows one special symbol at most.
  7. A reel strip has no more than 3 AUS symbols in sequence. Thus the window of each reel shows one or more symbols that are not AUS symbols.

docs.title: 5. Paytable
docs.text:
The values are credits for one way. A bet of 10 credits is necessary for these values.

A value of 0 means that the combination does not pay.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
1. The game examines each pay symbol independently.
  2. A combination of a pay symbol starts on reel 1. It continues on reel 2, reel 3 and the subsequent reels while each reel shows the pay symbol or a WILD symbol in one or more rows. The row is not important.
  3. The combination ends at the first reel that shows no such symbol. The number of reels in the combination is the "of a kind" number (OAK).
  4. On each reel of the combination, the game counts the pay symbol and the WILD symbols. The number of ways is the product of these counts.
  5. The pay of the symbol is the paytable value for its OAK number multiplied by the number of ways.
  6. Each pay symbol pays one time, for its longest combination only.
  7. Different pay symbols can pay in the same spin. The ways pays of the spin are the sum of the pays of all pay symbols.
  8. WILD substitutes for each pay symbol. One WILD symbol can be part of the combinations of different pay symbols in the same spin.
  9. WILD is not on reel 1. Thus each combination starts with a pay symbol on reel 1, and WILD symbols alone make no combination.
  10. A blocker symbol (KEY, FS, FISH) does not continue a combination.

docs.text:

  3. The game selects each value independently of the other values and of the stop positions.
  4. Each FISH symbol has a list of possible values. A weight table gives the probability of each value.
  5. The base game and each level of the free spins have their own weight tables.
  6. The value that a FISH symbol shows when the reels stop is the value that a KEY symbol collects.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
1. The game counts the KEY symbols in the full window.
  2. The game adds the values of all FISH symbols in the full window.
  3. Each KEY symbol pays the sum of the FISH values.
collect win = (sum of the FISH values in the window) x (number of KEY symbols in the window)
  1. The positions of the KEY symbols and of the FISH symbols are not important. A FISH symbol can be on the same reel as the KEY symbol, or on a reel to the left or to the right.
  2. If the window shows no KEY symbol, the FISH symbols pay nothing.
  3. If the window shows a KEY symbol and no FISH symbol, the collect win is 0.
  4. The collect win does not depend on the ways pays. One spin can have ways pays and a collect win.
  5. In the base game, KEY is on reels 1, 2, 3. FISH3 is on reel 4. FISH4 is on reel 5.

docs.title: 9. Win of a spin
docs.text:
The game calculates a spin in this sequence:

  1. Select the stop position of each reel.
  2. Select the value of each FISH symbol.
  3. Calculate the ways pays (section 6).
  4. Calculate the collect win (section 8).
  5. In the free spins, apply the level multiplier (section 11).
  6. In the base game, count the FS symbols (section 10).
base spin win = ways pays + collect win

docs.title: 10. Free spins trigger
docs.text:
1. FS is a scatter symbol. The game counts the FS symbols in the full window. The positions are not important.
  2. One reel shows one FS symbol at most. Thus the window shows 5 FS symbols at most.
  3. The table shows the number of initial free spins.

  1. Fewer than 3 FS symbols have no function.
  2. The FS symbol has no pay of its own.
  3. The base spin that starts the free spins pays its ways pays and its collect win as usual.
  4. The free spins start after the game pays the base spin.

docs.title: Reels and symbols
docs.text:
1. The free spins use the bonus reel strips.
  2. The bonus reel strips have no WILD symbol and no FS symbol.
  3. The bonus reel strips have 70 FISH symbols and 5 KEY symbols. The base reel strips have 24 FISH symbols and 3 KEY symbols.
  4. The free spins cannot start more free spins. There is no retrigger.
  5. The rules for ways pays (section 6), fish values (section 7) and collect (section 8) are the same as in the base game.

docs.title: Levels
docs.text:
Level KEY symbols necessary (total in the free spins) Spins Multiplier 1 none 10 / 15 / 20 (initial free spins) x1 2 3 8 x2 3 6 8 x5 4 9 8 x10
  1. The initial free spins are level 1.
  2. The game has a KEY counter. The counter starts at 0 when the free spins start. KEY symbols of the base spin do not count.
  3. Each KEY symbol that lands in a free spin adds 1 to the counter. The counter does not decrease and does not go back to 0 between levels.
  4. The game examines the counter only when all spins of the current level are complete.
  5. If the counter is equal to or more than the threshold of the subsequent level, the subsequent level starts with its number of spins.
  6. If the counter is less than the threshold, the free spins end.
  7. The levels come in sequence. The game does not skip a level, also when the counter is more than the threshold of a higher level.
  8. KEY symbols that land in a level count for all subsequent thresholds.
  9. Spins do not move from one level to the subsequent level. Each level has its own number of spins.
  10. After the last spin of level 4, the free spins end.

docs.title: Level multiplier
docs.text:
1. Each level has a multiplier.
  2. The level multiplier multiplies the full win of the spin: the ways pays and the collect win.
  3. The multiplier of a level applies to each spin of that level.
  4. The multiplier does not change the number of KEY symbols.
free spin win = level multiplier x (ways pays + collect win)

docs.title: Fish values in the free spins
docs.text: Each level uses its own weight tables for the fish values (section 7).

docs.title: End of the free spins
docs.text:
1. The free spins end when the counter is not sufficient for the subsequent level, or when the top level is complete.
  2. The win of the free spins is the sum of the wins of all free spins.
  3. The game adds this win to the balance. Then the game goes back to the base reel strips.

docs.title: 13. Questions and answers
docs.text:
Can one spin have ways pays, a collect win and a free spins trigger? Yes. The game pays all of them.

Does a KEY symbol pay if there is no FISH symbol? No. In the free spins, the KEY symbol adds 1 to the KEY counter in each case.

Does a FISH symbol pay if there is no KEY symbol? No.

Can two or more KEY symbols land in one spin? Yes. KEY is on reels 1, 2, 3 in the base game and on reels 1, 2, 3 in the free spins. One reel shows one KEY symbol at most. Thus one spin can show up to 3 KEY symbols in the base game and up to 3 KEY symbols in the free spins. The probability of two or more KEY symbols is 0.47% for each base spin and 1.23% for each free spin. Each KEY symbol collects each FISH value. In the free spins, each KEY symbol adds 1 to the counter.

Does the multiplier of a level apply to the ways pays? Yes. It applies to the full win of each spin of that level.

Do KEY symbols of level 1 count for level 3? Yes. The counter is the total for the full free spins.

Can the free spins go from level 1 to level 3 directly? No. Level 2 comes first.

Can the free spins start again in the free spins? No. The bonus reel strips have no FS symbol.

Does the FISH value change between the spin start and the reel stop? The game selects the values at the start of the spin. The reels show the new values 500 ms after the spin start, before the first reel stops.

docs.title: 14. Presentation rules of the playable game
docs.text:
These rules do not change the result of a spin.

  • Fish value swap. The reels start at the wager. The FISH symbols show their new values 500 ms after the wager. The reels are in motion at this time. No reel stops before the swap.
  • KEY anticipation. If a KEY symbol lands on reel 1, 2 or 3, reels 4 and 5 spin longer and show a glow.
  • FS anticipation. If 2 FS symbols are in the window, each subsequent reel that can show an FS symbol spins longer and shows a glow.
  • Kraken slow motion. This step applies to a reel that shows the KEY anticipation and that has a kraken symbol (FISH4) on its strip. The last 18 symbols before the stop move on the true reel strip. If a kraken symbol comes into the window in this part, the reel decreases its speed to 2.8 symbols for each second. The kraken symbol then stops in the window, or it goes out at the bottom of the window and the reel increases its speed again. A spotlight frame follows the kraken symbol. The step applies to the two kraken values.
  • Win presentation. The game shows the ways pays first, then the collect, then the level multiplier. This sequence does not change the win.

docs.title: Version 2.0.0: the redesign
docs.text:
Iteration 6 changed the structure of the game. These were the steps.

  1. New reel rules. The gap between special symbols increased from 2 to 3. The design got a limit of 3 AUS symbols in sequence. A new generator makes strips that obey the two rules.
  2. KEY symbols. The base game got one KEY symbol on each of reels 1, 2 and 3 (before: one KEY on reel 3). The mean number of KEY symbols for each base spin increased from 0.04 to 0.12.
  3. First result. With no other change, the RTP was 105.6%. The base collect was 62.6%, and the kraken gave 48% of this. The free spins gave 8.6%.
  4. Free spins trigger. The target was 1 in 175. Whole FS symbols on strips of 100 symbols cannot give this value. The selected layout has FS symbols on all 5 reels (3, 2, 2, 2, 2) and gives 1 in 171.66.
  5. Levels. With one KEY symbol on each of bonus reels 1 to 3, levels 2, 3 and 4 came in 12%, 1.8% and 0.3% of the free spins. With 2 / 2 / 1 KEY symbols on bonus reels 1 / 2 / 3, they come in 34%, 13% and 6%. This is almost the same as in version 1.1.0. The thresholds did not change.
  6. Golden kraken. The weights of the two kraken values changed from 2 : 1 to 8 : 1, in the base game and in the free spins. The mean kraken value is now 666.7 credits (before: 1000). The result was an RTP of 101.9%.

docs.text:

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text:
One KEY symbol on each of base reels 1, 2 and 3. A KEY symbol lands 1 in 8.7 base spins. Two or three KEY symbols can land in one spin. Then each KEY symbol collects each FISH value.

The kraken stays on the base reel strips. The KEY anticipation on reels 4 and 5 has a purpose only if the large fish are there. The kraken gives 26% RTP in the base game. A KEY symbol and the kraken land together 1 in 217 base spins.

Golden kraken weights 30 : 1 in the base game. With weights 2 : 1, the kraken gave 48% RTP in the base game, and the total was too high. Version 2.0.0 changed the weights to 8 : 1. Version 2.7.0 changed them to 30 : 1, because the larger paytable took RTP from the collect. The usual kraken pays 500 credits. The golden kraken pays 2000 credits.

The balance of version 2.0.0 came from the small base fish. In that version, the paytable and the free spins kept their value. The free spins were less frequent than before, so their value for each trigger did not decrease.

The balance of version 2.1.0 came from the 5 OAK pays. The reel strips with patterns give fewer long ways. Larger 5 OAK pays put this RTP back into the ways pays, so that the RTP of each component stays almost the same.

2 / 2 / 1 KEY symbols on bonus reels 1 / 2 / 3. This gives 0.20 KEY symbols for each free spin, the same as in version 1.1.0. The levels keep their frequency.

The AUS symbols give 12% RTP in the base game. Before version 2.6.0, they gave 22%. The low pay symbols make frequent small wins. The PIC symbols now give the larger part of the ways pays.

PIC1 is rare and pays the most. PIC1 has 7 / 2 / 4 / 6 / 5 symbols on base reels 1 to 5. A PIC1 win needs reel 2, where PIC1 has few symbols. The pays of PIC1 are 5 / 25 / 100 credits for 3 / 4 / 5 OAK.

Eight spins for levels 2 to 4. With 10 spins, level 4 was too frequent.

Bonus reels with more PIC symbols. The bonus reel strips have no WILD symbol. More PIC symbols give more ways pays in the free spins.

The best fish values are on level 1. Each free spins feature plays level 1. Thus each feature has a chance of the high FISH3 values and of the golden kraken. On the higher levels, the multiplier gives the large wins, and the high values are harder to get. The mean FISH3 value decreases from 133.0 credits on level 1 to 63.0 credits on level 4. The golden kraken has weights of 2 : 1 on level 1 and 64 : 1 on level 4.

docs.title: Possible subsequent changes
docs.text:
• A variant with the kraken only in the free spins: remove FISH4 from the base reel strips and put that RTP into the free spins (mean free spins win approximately 80 x bet).
  • A higher volatility variant: decrease the trigger frequency and increase the level multipliers.
  • A win limit, if the market requires one.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Four implementations calculate the game:

Implementation File Method Excel workbook excel/TacklinTheKraken_TheoCalc.xlsx Formulas. Exact. Exact calculator gamemath/exact_calc.py Python with exact fractions Game engine and simulator web/js/engine.js, sim/simulate.mjs Monte Carlo simulation with the engine of the playable game C++ simulator sim_cpp/krakensim.cpp Monte Carlo simulation with its own C++ engine. It made the simulation results of this document.

The script tools/verify_all.py compares them. It does these checks:

  1. The reel strips obey the design rules. The script also examines each window of each reel: one special symbol at most, and one or more symbols that are not AUS symbols.
  2. The inputs of the workbook are equal to the configuration file.
  3. The results of the workbook are equal to the results of the exact calculator.
  4. The script changes the inputs in a copy of the workbook and does check 3 again. It uses three changed configurations:
    • A: new pays (with 1 OAK and 2 OAK pays), new fish values and weights, new level thresholds, spins and multipliers, multiplier rule fish.
    • B: new reel strips with KEY symbols on all 5 reels, more FS symbols, a bet of 25 credits.
    • C: reel strips with random manual changes that do not obey the gap rule.
  5. The JavaScript engine and an independent Python evaluator give the same result for 40,000 random spins.
  6. The C++ simulator and the JavaScript engine give the same result for 100,000 random spins.
  7. The simulation agrees with the exact values: the total RTP, each RTP component, the trigger frequency and the level probabilities.

Microsoft Excel also calculated the workbook of version 2.7.0. The result was the same as the exact calculator (total RTP 96.2000313739%).

docs.title: Limits of the verification
docs.text:
• The simulation has a standard error of 0.001% RTP. It cannot show a difference smaller than this.
  • The random number generator of the playable game is xoshiro128**. The random number generator of the C++ simulator is xoshiro256++. They are not certified for real money play.
  • An independent test laboratory did not examine this model.
